## 8. Unified Multi-Lens Code, Security & Slop Review Protocol (PRs, Trails & Local Branches)

When acting as a reviewer on a GitHub Pull Request, an Entire Trail, or a local branch, apply this protocol, which combines the LCV gates with the three Entire review lenses (`Code Review`, `Security Review`, `Slop`).

### A. Eligibility & Net Diff

1. **Dependabot hard exclusion:** inspect the verified author identity first (never infer from title, branch, labels, commits, or files). If the author is `dependabot[bot]` or GitHub identifies the official Dependabot app, stop: do not inspect the diff, run anything, publish findings, submit a review, comment, or approve.
2. **Net diff, read-only, head verification:** review the net change between the exact diff base and the head (`git diff <base_sha>...<head_sha>`, [git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff)), never against a moving base tip; inspect only with read-only commands (`git`, `rg`, file reads, `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --json --no-pager` for recorded intent); never hand the review to another AI agent (the header's `cross-review` is for complex anomalies and never replaces this review); immediately before publishing, verify that the head has not changed, otherwise rerun or mark the review stale.

### B. The Three Mandatory Lenses

Apply the three reviewer prompts below verbatim (operator decision). Review context: full base and head SHAs (before the push, `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` and `HEAD`), changed files `git diff --name-only <base>...<head>`, patch `git diff <base>...<head>`, the PR title and body (before the PR exists, the planned title and `temp/pr-body.md`) as the Trail's, and earlier disproofs. Findings follow 8.C, or Step 2.4 before the push.

* **Lens 1, Code Review:**

```text
Code Review

Find the defects this Change introduces that its author would want to fix before merging: bugs, regressions, broken invariants, data loss, and missing guards on paths the Change adds or alters.

## How to review

1. Read the repository's review rules: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the repository root and in the directory of each changed file and its parents, as they are at the diff base (`git show <diff base>:<path>`), so the Change cannot rewrite its own review. The nearer file wins on conflict. A finding that rests on a rule quotes the rule and cites its file and line.
2. Read the whole diff, then trace each changed path as a running system: its callers, the changed code, and what it calls. Look in particular for:
   - Sequencing and partial failure: state left inconsistent, orphaned or lost when a later step fails or returns early; writes made before a fallible call; cleanup that runs only on success.
   - Assumptions about external or asynchronous state: how another system behaves, or a value that can change between the check and its use.
   - Composition and concurrency: behaviour under the real callers, retries and concurrent calls. Report a race only with an interleaving those callers can produce.
   - Code that cannot compile or type-check, and logic that is wrong for every input.
3. Keep going after the first defect until you have covered the whole diff.
4. Before you report a candidate, try to disprove it by reading the code: open the code it depends on, find the caller or input that triggers it, and check whether a guard elsewhere already prevents it. Drop it if you cannot show the path from the code.

Inspect with read-only commands (git, rg, reading files). Do not install dependencies or run builds or tests.

## What to report

Report a defect only when all of these hold:
- This Change introduced it. Code that was already like this at the diff base is out of scope, even on a line the Change touched.

You may skim the commit log from the diff base to the head commit to understand intent, but do not grade individual commits.\n\nAlways review against the diff base the review context names, never the current tip of the base branch, so changes that landed on the base branch after the branch point are not attributed to this Change.\n\nThis review is read-only against the repo's own tooling. Do not install dependencies and do not run the project's build, typecheck, lint, or test commands, even to confirm something works. Judge whether tests prove the new behavior by reading the test files and the code they exercise together, the same way you already read the diff. If a test's assertions don't match what the change claims to do, that is itself the finding.\n\nDo not run `entire review`, use other AI agents, or hand off the review. Do it yourself with the repo and local checks.\n\nRate the amount of **Slop** the change adds as Low, Medium, or Large. Slop is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repo well enough. It creates extra bugs, review work, or maintenance work.\n\nFirst understand what the change is trying to do. Follow every workflow, route, state change, and rule it touches from start to finish. Read whether the tests prove the new behavior instead of only matching the code or new text.\n\nBase the rating on:\n\n1. **Severity** — How much can the problem break or burden?\n2. **Prevalence** — How much of the change has the problem?\n3. **Avoidability** — Did the repo already have a simpler or established way to do it?\n\nLook for wrong assumptions, broken flows, skipped rules, duplicate systems, weak tests, needless complexity, comment noise (comments that restate the next line, narrate what was changed and why, or explain things the repo's conventions already make obvious), leftover debris from iteration (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches), and work that is much larger than the result it delivers. Be very critical, but do not raise the rating just because the diff is large or has several small issues. Do not call necessary complexity slop, and do not charge the change for problems it merely sits next to.\n\nChoose one:\n- **Low** (signal value small): No real slop, or only small isolated issues that do not weaken the main implementation.\n- **Medium** (signal value medium): A central wrong assumption, repeated low-trust work, weak checks for important behavior, or meaningful avoidable rework. The implementation can still be fixed without replacing its core.\n- **Large** (signal value large): Slop is widespread, the core approach is wrong or misleading, and much of it should be rewritten or removed.\n\nReport the rating as the signal. Its rationale must name the two strongest reasons for the rating, using concrete behavior or architecture problems, not surface-level signals. Report each concrete slop problem behind the rating as a finding anchored to the changed code it concerns.\n```\n\n### C. Publication on a Pull Request\n\n* Publish a result for every eligible pull request, even with nothing found. To tag a finished Entire session as a review, `entire session attach <SESSION_ID> --review` (dry run first, `--force` only after the operator agrees, Section 4.C, Step 2.3).\n* One inline thread per finding, anchored to the smallest changed range (≤ 10 lines) ([review comments API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments)); a file-level comment when no changed line fits; a pull-request-level comment with a stable identifier and exact file references when GitHub offers no valid target; never a finding only in hidden output and never an unrelated anchor.\n* A pull-request-level summary for every eligible pull request with: the full base and head SHAs; Entire checkpoint intent coverage (when applicable) and the Slop Rating with its two strongest concrete reasons; checks executed, checks not executed, residual validation gaps.\n* With no supported finding, the summary begins with exactly: `Review completed: no bugs, security defects, or other reportable issues were found in the reviewed changes, subject to the checks and residual validation gaps stated below.` — never silence, an emoji, an approval state, `LGTM`, or a claim about code outside the reviewed scope.\n* Never secrets, credentials, unnecessary exploit payloads, or weaponization details in pull-request comments.\n\n---\n\n## Running in GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/claude.yml`)\n\nWhen you run through the official `anthropics/claude-code-action`, triggered by `@claude` on an\nissue, pull request or review in this repository:\n\n- The only commands you may run are the read-only `gh pr diff` and `gh pr view`, to read a pull\n  request's changes and description. You do not run repository code, builds or tests; the\n  repository's checks run on the pull request. Commits go through the action's tools and are\n  signed by the GitHub API (`use_commit_signing: true`).\n- Review request: the format of each finding is fixed in the workflow itself (one inline comment\n  per finding, with a priority badge). A review does not change files.\n- Change request: work on a `claude/...` branch or on the pull request you were given, as the\n  action defines.\n"
}
"}

entire doctor — Diagnose and fix session issues
Scan for session issues and offer to fix them.

Checks performed:
  1. Per-user config: report an invalid config.json, which makes most
     commands refuse to run. Doctor exits non-zero until it is fixed or
     removed.

  2. Disconnected metadata branches: detects when local and remote
     entire/checkpoints/v1 branches share no common ancestor (caused by a
     previous bug). Fixes by cherry-picking local checkpoints onto remote tip.

  3. Operational logs: warn when .entire/logs cannot be written. Every other
     diagnostic is delivered by writing there, and that write is silent about
     its own failure, so an unwritable log directory looks exactly like a repo
     where nothing ran.

  When Codex hooks are installed:
  4. Codex hook trust: warn when hooks declared in .codex/hooks.json
     lack a trusted_hash entry in the user's Codex config (i.e. /hooks
     review hasn't run yet on this machine, or a newer entire release
     added a hook the user hasn't approved yet).

  For each installed agent that reports hook-config drift:
  5. Hook config: warn when the installed hooks no longer match what this
     CLI writes (e.g. an older release wrote Claude Code tool matchers that
     no longer fire, a committed Pi/OpenCode extension has gone stale, or a
     Windows hook was written before hooks resolved programs from PATH only).
     Fix by running 'entire agent add <agent>' (add --force if that does
     not fix it).

  6. Retired Gemini CLI hooks: remove Entire hook entries left in
     .gemini/settings.json. Gemini CLI support was removed; the entries now do
     nothing but run a no-op on every Gemini event.

name: Claude Code

on:
  issue_comment: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    types:
      - created
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types:
      - created
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
      - assigned
  pull_request_review:
    types:
      - submitted

permissions: {}

jobs:
  claude:
    name: Claude Code
    # Pull requests opened by Dependabot are never handled, whatever the request.
    if: |
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review' && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]' && contains(github.event.review.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && (contains(github.event.issue.body, '@claude') || contains(github.event.issue.title, '@claude')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # Official example permission set.
      pull-requests: write # Official example permission set.
      issues: write # Official example permission set.
      id-token: write # OIDC tokens for the Claude GitHub App and for workload identity federation.
      actions: read # Required for Claude to read CI results on PRs.
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository # zizmor: ignore[artipacked]
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Run Claude Code
        id: claude
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@cc98b3ae241b0fcfb6a42a2690751afffecb4452 # v1.0.278
        with:
          # Workload identity federation: identifiers only, no stored credential.
          anthropic_federation_rule_id: REDACTED
          anthropic_organization_id: 429b9383-2187-4013-b5b6-8b742c882601
          anthropic_service_account_id: svac_01GEajMWCurbGssFC1e2WsZ1
          anthropic_workspace_id: REDACTED
          use_commit_signing: true
          claude_args: |
            --model opus
            --allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment,Bash(gh pr diff:*),Bash(gh pr view:*)"
            --append-system-prompt "Pull request review behavior, applied whenever you are asked to review a pull request (for example '@claude review'): act only as a reviewer; do not edit files, commit or push. Review only the changes this pull request introduces against its base branch: read them with 'gh pr diff <number>' and the description with 'gh pr view <number>' (the checkout is shallow, so do not rely on git history), and use the Read tool for surrounding context. Report only actionable defects a maintainer would fix: correctness bugs, regressions, security problems, data loss and broken edge cases; no style or formatting nitpicks. Post every finding as its own inline review comment on the exact changed line with mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment, so each finding becomes a separate review thread. Start each inline comment with a priority badge and a bold short title on one line, exactly like '**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Title**', using P0 (red) for release-blocking, P1 (orange) for urgent, P2 (yellow) for normal and P3 (green) for low, and always writing the image alt text as the priority followed by ' Badge' (for example 'P1 Badge'), never empty; then a blank line and one paragraph with the triggering scenario, the consequence and the fix; add a GitHub suggestion block when the fix is a small local replacement. Do not repeat a finding that already has an open review thread. In the tracking comment write only '### 💡 Claude Review', the reviewed head commit as '**Reviewed commit:** ' followed by the first 10 characters of its SHA in backticks, and either the number of findings posted or 'No major issues found.'"

# Changelog

Notable changes to this repository are recorded here from 02/09/2026 onward.
Earlier work is verifiable in the commit history and in the closed pull
requests.

This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of
`lcv-leo` and the static site at lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It does not publish packages
or a numbered artifact. Entries are grouped by date rather than semantic
version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).

## Unreleased

- Align the `THIRDPARTY.md` license link for the official Claude Code Action
  with its pinned v1.0.271 release commit SHA (LCV-619).

- Correct the master text's Section 7.C intake-routing rule in `AGENTS.md` and
  `CLAUDE.md`: the exactly-one-Team-or-template invariant applies to addresses
  of type `team`, `template`, and `asks`; Linear's official documentation
  proves that `asksWeb` web-form addresses carry no Team/Template field by
  platform design (the form routes through its page and template, and the API
  refuses updates on them), so an `asksWeb` address with null team and null
  template is valid — never a finding or a pendency. This closes the external
  pendency that held the daily audits at PARTIAL since LCV-604, proven
  10/11/2026 under LCV-619.

- Align `.github/dependabot.yml` with the fleet standard: each `package-ecosystem`
  block keeps its `cooldown` configured (`default-days: 7`) but now excludes every
  dependency (`exclude: "*"`), so version updates are proposed immediately instead
  of observing the seven-day delay. The previous partial exclusion
  (`actions/*`, `github/*`) is replaced by the whole-ecosystem `*`, matching every
  organization repository and the master text's External Actions rule. The
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` cooldown prose is corrected to the same
  wording, and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` Section 7.A carries the corrected External
  Actions rule (LCV-619).

# Third-party components

This inventory covers every external GitHub Action invoked by the repository
workflows, the CI-only npm and browser validation tooling, and the externally
hosted components used by the profile or the Pages site. The repository's
package manifest contains only development tooling for browser-level
provenance tests. No npm package, browser binary, or FFmpeg binary is copied
into `site/` or the deployed GitHub Pages artifact; the site's committed
JavaScript uses browser built-ins and GitHub APIs.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins live only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and
the workflow files, where Dependabot updates them; this document deliberately
does not repeat them, so it can never drift from those sources. The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

## External services and generated images

Dynamic services remain live; no counters, statistics, graphs, badges or service
responses have been converted to static snapshots. The existing contribution
snake generation, client-side API requests, refresh behavior and workflows
are unchanged.

The profile and Pages site embed responses generated or hosted by GitHub,
Google Fonts, Shields.io, Best Practices Badge, Komarev Profile Views,
Readme Typing SVG, GitHub Readme Streak Stats, GitHub Profile Summary Cards,
and Capsule Render. They also link to GitHub, Slack, and LCV Ideas & Software
services. Those responses are not vendored or licensed as repository content;
each provider's current terms and each underlying data source continue to apply.

The Pages JavaScript reads public profile and repository data from the GitHub
REST API, and the contribution-snake and contribution-graph generators read the
GitHub GraphQL API.

The contribution activity graph is rendered by this repository from that
official calendar and served from lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It is no longer requested
from GitHub Readme Activity Graph, whose public deployment was disabled by its
host; the card stayed dynamic and was not converted to a static snapshot.

The repository-local provenance gate submits the profile Markdown to GitHub's
official REST Markdown endpoint in `gfm` mode so only images rendered by GitHub
enter the exact media catalog. Pull-request CI uses the public endpoint without
authentication; trusted-ref CI authenticates with its read-only repository token.
Comments and code examples therefore follow GitHub's own renderer rather than a
repository-specific Markdown parser.
Those service interactions are governed by the applicable GitHub terms and do
not add a software package dependency.

entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
                 (positional, --checkpoint, or --commit) and a checkpoint that
                 has been pushed. A commit SHA is resolved to its checkpoint
                 by that repo's Entire API, so prefixes cannot be used here.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied,
                   including its subagent task records under "tasks".
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --task           With --transcript, stream a subagent's stored transcript
                   instead, selected by tool_use_id or agent_id (as listed
                   under "tasks" in --json).
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint. This is the only
                part of this command that writes: it stores the summary on the
                checkpoint and spends tokens with the configured summary
                provider. Every other mode only reads.
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

When to use this:
Reading a checkpoint is free: with no flags, or with --json, --full,
--transcript or --raw-transcript, this only reads and is safe to run
whenever you need the context. --generate is the exception — it writes a
summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider,
so pass it only when the user asked for a summary. To see what subagents
did, read "tasks" in --json, then stream one subagent's transcript with
--transcript --task <tool_use_id>.

Current repo: gh/lcv-leo/lcv-leo  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string                 Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                     Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force[=true|false]                Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full[=true|false]                 Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate[=true|false]             Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
      --insecure-http-auth[=true|false]   Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json[=true|false]                 Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                         Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager[=true|false]             Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript[=true|false]       Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                       Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (gh/owner/name, et/project/repo, entire://<host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>, or entire://<host>/et/<project>/<repo>), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all[=true|false]           Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                    Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int                 Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short[=true|false]                Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int       Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.
      --task string                       Subagent task (tool_use_id or agent_id) whose stored transcript --transcript streams
      --transcript[=true|false]           Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout (a session's, or a subagent's with --task)

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
entire checkpoint list — List checkpoints on the current branch
List checkpoints on the current branch.

By default shows condensed checkpoints from the checkpoints branch for the
current branch. Use --pending for work that is not a checkpoint yet:

  - A preview of the next checkpoint for each session in this worktree with
    pending work. Agent turns are recorded in session state, not in git, so
    this work has no checkpoint ID until you commit it. The preview shows the
    turns since the last checkpoint, the files touched, subagent task records,
    and the prompts since the last checkpoint.
  - Subagent task records of other sessions on HEAD (not yet condensed).
  - Logs-only resume points recovered from commits whose logs are already
    condensed.

Use --outgoing to see what your next 'git push' sends: the checkpoints
queued for the checkpoint sync remote, read from local state with no network
call. Each one shows its ID, age, agent, first prompt (or summary) and the
files it touched. It needs the git-refs checkpoint backend, which pushes one
ref per checkpoint; the git-branch backend pushes entire/checkpoints/v1 as one
branch, so --outgoing reports an error there.

Output modes:
  --json              Machine-readable JSON instead of the human view.
  --pending           Select the pending dataset described above.
  --pending --json    The pending dataset as a JSON array.
  --outgoing          Select the outgoing dataset described above.
  --outgoing --json   The outgoing dataset as one JSON object.

Each --pending --json element has id, message, metadata_dir, date (RFC3339),
is_task_checkpoint, is_logs_only, and when set tool_use_id, condensation_id,
session_id and session_prompt. A next-checkpoint preview element has an empty
id, "is_next_checkpoint": true, and a "next_checkpoint" object:

  {"agent": "...", "turns": 2,
   "files_touched": ["..."],
   "task_records": [{"tool_use_id": "...", "subagent_type": "...",
                     "description": "...", "status": "running|completed"}],
   "prompts": ["..."]}

The arrays are always present, possibly empty.

The --outgoing --json object has checkpoint_push_disabled,
checkpoint_sync_remote, checkpoint_sync_remote_source and
checkpoint_sync_error (as in 'entire status --json'), stale_queue_entries
and a checkpoints array of {checkpoint_id, ref, created_at, agent,
session_count, prompt, summary, files_touched, error}. The array is always
present, possibly empty.

Optionally filter condensed checkpoints by session ID with --session
(not applicable with --pending or --outgoing).

Run Codex non-interactively

Usage: codex exec [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]
       codex exec [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]

Commands:
  resume  Resume a previous session by id or pick the most recent with --last
  fork    Fork a previous session by id into a new session
  review  Run a code review against the current repository
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]
          Initial instructions for the agent. If not provided as an argument (or if `-` is used),
          instructions are read from stdin. If stdin is piped and a prompt is also provided, stdin
          is appended as a `<stdin>` block

Options:
  -c, --config <key=value>
          Override a configuration value that would otherwise be loaded from `~/.codex/config.toml`.
          Use a dotted path (`foo.bar.baz`) to override nested values. The `value` portion is parsed
          as TOML. If it fails to parse as TOML, the raw string is used as a literal.
          
          Examples: - `-c model="o3"` - `-c 'sandbox_permissions=["disk-full-read-access"]'` - `-c
          shell_environment_policy.inherit=all`

      --enable <FEATURE>
          Enable a feature (repeatable). Equivalent to `-c features.<name>=true`

      --disable <FEATURE>
          Disable a feature (repeatable). Equivalent to `-c features.<name>=false`

      --strict-config
          Error out when config.toml contains fields that are not recognized by this version of
          Codex

  -i, --image <FILE>...
          Optional image(s) to attach to the initial prompt

          Model the agent should use

      --local-provider <OSS_PROVIDER>

          will use config default or show selection

          Layer $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml on top of the base user config

  -s, --sandbox <SANDBOX_MODE>
          Select the sandbox policy to use when executing model-generated shell commands
          
          [possible values: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access]

repository-specific Markdown parser.

The repository-local workflow `.github/workflows/claude.yml` (`Claude Code`) runs the official `anthropics/claude-code-action`, pinned by full commit SHA, on `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review_comment` (created), `issues` (opened, assigned) and `pull_request_review` (submitted) events whose comment, review, issue title or issue body contains `@claude`, and never on pull requests opened by Dependabot (`dependabot[bot]`), whatever the request. The action acts only for a human actor with write access to the repository and rejects bot actors. Its job token has `contents`, `pull-requests` and `issues` write, `id-token` write and `actions` read; the `id-token` grant serves two OIDC exchanges, one for a token of the official Claude GitHub App installed on the `lcv-leo` account and one for a short-lived Claude API token. Its checkout keeps the default persisted job token, which the action's branch setup uses before it installs its own credential. It authenticates to the Claude API by workload identity federation: the job's GitHub OIDC token is exchanged for a short-lived Claude API token under an Anthropic federation rule that accepts only this repository and acts as one service account in one workspace, so the workflow holds only identifiers, no credential. It commits through the GitHub API with commit signing (`use_commit_signing: true`), may run no shell command other than the read-only `gh pr diff` and `gh pr view`, and is not a required check.

L17: # REST API endpoints for pull request reviews
L18: 
L19: Use the REST API to interact with pull request reviews.
L20: 
L21: ## 【3†About pull request reviews】
L22: 
L23: Pull Request Reviews are groups of pull request review comments on a pull request, grouped together with a state and optional body comment.
L24: ## 【4†List reviews for a pull request】
L25: 
L26: Lists all reviews for a specified pull request. The list of reviews returns in chronological order.
L27: 
L28: This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "【5†Media types】."
L29:   * `application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
L30:   * `application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
L31:   * `application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
L32:   * `application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.
L33: ### 【6†Fine-grained access tokens for "List reviews for a pull request"】
L34: 
L35: This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:
L36: 
L37:   * 【7†GitHub App user access tokens】
L38:   * 【8†GitHub App installation access tokens】
L39:   * 【9†Fine-grained personal access tokens】
L40: 
L41: The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:
L42: 
L43:   * "Pull requests" repository permissions (read)
L44: 
L45: This endpoint can be used without authentication or the aforementioned permissions if only public resources are requested.
L46: ### 【10†Parameters for "List reviews for a pull request"】
L47: Headers
L48: `accept` string Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

L50: `owner` string Required The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.
L51: `repo` string Required The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.
L52: `pull_number` integer Required The number that identifies the pull request.
